note: Sectioned-bill GST anchor, recap printed -- the counterpart to bug_260528_0016. This BC Hydro bill taxes each section separately (TAXES ON ACCOUNT CHARGES * GST 5% $0.68, TAXES ON ELECTRICITY CHARGES * GST 5% on $49.72 $2.49) AND prints the bill-level total in a recap (TAX SUMMARY GST 5% on $63.22 $3.17). gst_amount must be the recap 3.17, never one section's line and never the 6.34 grand sum of all three printed GST amounts. This document motivated the 2026-07-23 prompt fix but was never added to the corpus; it is the only doc pinning the recap branch. || NOT asserted here: invoice_description, which flips between 'Electricity utility charges' and 'Electricity charges and account set-up' run to run. || Narrative fields (diagnosis_solution, diagnosis_solution_zh_hant, recommendation, recommendation_zh_hant, warranty) are asserted '' by design: build_write_values blanks all five for the municipal bucket, so these are the live counterpart of the offline bucket-gate test -- a non-empty value here means the gate broke, or bill_type misclassified this bill as commercial. || invoice_date NOT asserted -- OPEN PRODUCT ISSUE: n=10 gave the printed 2026-06-17 x9 and today's date x1, i.e. both date twins fail together about 1 run in 10 and today is written instead. Lower rate than bug_260528_0016 but the same defect. || number_of_days 28 IS asserted from 2026-08-18 and this doc is the A2 anchor. It used to give 13 and 28 for the same bill (28 x9 / 13 x5 at n=14), which fed the tenant utility-sharing calculation. The bill's own printed period settles it: 2026-05-19 to 2026-06-15 is 28 days inclusive, and 13 is exactly May 19-31 -- the count of the period's FIRST month only. gates.evaluate now lets the period dates arbitrate the count when the two disagree by more than a metered count honestly can (max(10 days, 15%)); a count merely differing from the span, as on the water bills, is kept. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20).
